content:
talia: deploy-bot reports a Canary p95 jitter spike on v3.5.1. Auto-rollback attempted but blocked by a targeted pin on NA-dedicated-2. We need a rapid call: let deploy-bot force revert (risking customer-facing change) or do a narrow manual mitigation? @ops_oncall @ravi

deploy-bot: [system] canary metrics | p95 520ms (threshold 350ms) | error_rate 1.1% | auto-rollback: attempted -> blocked (targeted-pin: NA-dedicated-2). see: https://telemetry.internal/release/1767784444

ravi: this lines up with yesterday's dynamic-batching change. The spike is more pronounced when sequence lengths > 1024.

jen: We have two options: 1) let deploy-bot force a full rollback (will unpin NA-dedicated-2) — needs exec approval; 2) perform a canary-only revert of the batching change and then roll a conservative 15% fallback on NA-dedicated-2. Ops takes ~18m for unpin + safety checklist.

ops_oncall: confirm. Full unpin requires validation of customer contracts and escalation. We can do a partial traffic split faster.

pmaria: If we unpin, we'll need a short notice to affected accounts. Partial fallback is lower risk.

Sanjay: I'm leaning partial fallback + canary revert. Less disruptive and still addresses tail latency. I'll own the rollback if we go that route.

Talia: Agreed. Sanjay proceed with canary revert and then coordinate with ops for traffic split if metrics improve. Record the decision in release notes.

deploy-bot: [action] manual-rollback-requested by talia at 1767784444. Notifying ops and oncall.

Sanjay: kicking off canary revert now:
```
infra/rollout toggle --service=inference --flag=dynamic_batching_v2 --state=off --scope=canary
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-canary
```

Sanjay: revert started 1767784500. streaming health checks here.

[~7 minutes later]

deploy-bot: canary metrics update | p95 320ms | error_rate 0.3% | status: stabilized

Sanjay: revert successful. 6 pods rotated. Requesting approval to apply 15% fallback on NA-dedicated-2 to v3.5.0 (prev stable).

ops_oncall: applying routing change now. will signal once done.

[~5 minutes later]

ops_oncall: routing applied: NA-dedicated-2 -> 15% to v3.5.0, 85% v3.5.1 (pinned). Observability: p95 for NA-dedicated-2 down to 340ms. No customer-facing alerts.

pmaria: drafting comms: "We observed increased tail latency during a canary for v3.5.1 due to dynamic batching. We reverted the canary and applied a small traffic fallback for NA-dedicated-2 while we finalize a fix. No customer action required." will post to status page in 10m.

ravi: follow-ups: add sequence-length gated timeout, and add a rollback-safety flag to auto-rollback that respects pinned pools by escalating to oncall rather than forcing unpin. Also run a stress test for long sequences.

jen: I'll own the postmortem if the fallback persists. Let's collect traces from the canary and dedicated pool over next 2hrs.

Talia: thanks. Closing manual rollback thread after status post. :white_check_mark:

[closing log]
deploy-bot: [log] manual-rollback completed at 1767785120. canary revert executed, partial fallback applied, comms queued.
